QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_61

question.text: What risk management framework governs arbitrage positions in ETIRD?

answer.text: Arbitrage positions remain subject to clearing-corporation risk management, including margin, MTM settlement, and position limits; portfolio offsets may affect margin only where the applicable framework provides it
Arbitrage positions are exempt from all risk management requirements
Arbitrageurs must deposit double margin compared to other participants
There is no specific framework; arbitrageurs follow no rules

explanation.text: The Logic: Arbitrage is the simultaneous execution of offsetting trades. ETIRD arbitrage positions are subject to standard clearing-corporation risk management — initial margin, MTM settlement, position monitoring, and SPAN-based portfolio margining. Cross-margining is a general clearing-corporation feature available where the framework supports it. The Trap: No participant is exempt from risk management. Double margin is punitive and not applied. The workbook does not promise blanket cash-and-futures cross-margining for arbitrageurs — any margin offset depends on what the applicable framework permits. Note: Position offsets across trading venues, and SPAN-recognised spreads, are the two main sources of margin efficiency for arbitrageurs. The benefit is mechanical, not status-based.
